sections.title: Employment Contract
sections.text:
S.E.E.S. leader Makoto Yuki met another self on the night of the full moon.

Pull the trigger, and the Persona is released from within—blazing flames draw the enemy into oblivion.

sections.text:
Makoto Yuki. Registered in March of 1102 at the Atrium Notary Office as kin to a citizen of Laterano; admitted to Saint Marcel Comprehensive School pursuant to Article 34 of the appendix to the Charter of Lateran Citizens' Rights.
Teacher's remarks: Makoto Yuki conducts himself calmly, gets along with his classmates, respects his teachers and elders, and takes an active part in community service, where he has earned unanimous praise during volunteer work. May he persevere and press on, and take one more step even from the top of the hundred-foot pole.

sections.title: Archive File 1
sections.text:
Makoto keeps a low profile and says little, and for a time we worried whether he could settle into school life in Laterano. His conduct since has proved that worry entirely unnecessary.
On the day of the school anniversary festival, Aigis came to Amiya for help: she could not find Makoto. For reasons of her own, Amiya happened to be looking for her class's homeroom teacher at the time, so the two of them set out together on a festival-day search. The celebrations each class puts on take wildly different forms, and if things go wrong the festival can devolve into a hostage-exchange prank contest; Aigis seemed worried that Makoto might land in trouble. Amiya reassured her that, to prevent exactly that, the school had strongly encouraged a return to traditional festivities this year—so the worst danger Makoto faced was a blood-sugar swing from excessive carbohydrates along the endless row of dessert stalls.
Just as Amiya predicted, the two of them picked up Makoto's trail on the dessert street: nearly every stall said he had been helping there only moments before. By their accounts, Makoto first whipped cream at the ice cream stall, then went to the canelé stall to mix batter, then filled cream puffs, and was last seen piping chestnut cream at the Mont Blanc stall. At last, Aigis and Amiya found him at the crêpe stall at the end of the street, where a long queue had formed. He was making the "Ascension Cumulonimbus Crêpe," whose selling point was a filling piled as high as a cumulonimbus cloud in May. The student minding the stall begged Aigis not to take him away: "I know Makoto isn't in our class, but the customers have queued this long for his special crêpes..."
"Huh, is the crêpe guy going off shift?" asked a blue-haired Sankta waiting in the queue, then turned to her red-haired Liberi companion. "Fiammetta, your luck is terrible."
"What's that got to do with me?" the Liberi retorted, then turned back and asked, "Excuse me—we've been queuing a long time. Could you really not make two more... or even just one?"
The student minding the stall looked at Aigis and Makoto with a troubled face.
"If Makoto cannot leave, then I will remain here to be with him." Aigis nodded.
"Aigis, won't you come look for the teacher with me?" Amiya said, a little troubled. "I was hoping that if you helped, the two of us could search together..."
"Aigis, go help Amiya find the Doctor." Makoto said calmly as he spread the batter. "Then come back here for me. I'll be waiting."
"Don't you have other stalls to get to, Makoto? Come to think of it, why are you helping at so many of them...?" Amiya asked, curious.
"I'll be here later too. Friends asked me to." Makoto answered as he laid out the fruit.
"Ohh, I think I saw you at the cream puff and Mont Blanc stalls earlier too." the blue-haired Sankta said. "You've got that many friends?"
"It's fine." Makoto poured a quintuple helping of maple syrup over the top of the crêpe and handed it to the customer who had waited so long.
Later, all the transfer students heard what had happened on the festival day, and apparently discussed it back at the dorm—not why Makoto had been helping out everywhere, which they had long since stopped finding strange, but when on earth he had learned to make so many different desserts. They never reached a consensus. The learning ability of the leader of S.E.E.S. is, it seems, genuinely a mystery.

sections.title: Archive File 2
sections.text:
Sports clubs are said to have invited Makoto at one point, but perhaps because most of this school's athletic clubs revolve around firearms or firearm-like disciplines, he joined none of them. When it came to extracurriculars, he had other options.
One day after school, Makoto asked Yukari whether she knew of anywhere nearby to work part-time. Yukari was a little surprised. "The school looks after us pretty well, so there's not much need to work... Is there something you want to buy?"
Makoto only nodded, without explaining further. Ambriel, passing by, overheard the two of them; her eyes lit up and she sidled over with a grin, asking whether Makoto was free today. It was common knowledge among the students that Ambriel often took part-time work, or odd commissions from classmates, to buy whatever was in fashion.
Makoto accepted Ambriel's proposal, and she led him and Yukari to—the most popular arcade in the Saint Marcel district. Bypassing fifty kinds of outlandish shooting games, she dragged the two of them to a side-scrolling action cabinet.
"This job—well, all right, it's actually a commission from Randall in your class. He wants the event bonus for this game, and to trade for it you need the time-attack clear trophies on all six of the big maps, co-op mode included." Ambriel spread her hands, a lollipop in her mouth. "As you can see, hardly anyone plays this. Team up with me and we'll split the fee fifty-fifty. How about it?"
Makoto studied the screen in thought, then finally nodded to Ambriel. Seeing that the two of them would need a while to find their rhythm, Yukari decided to pick a few of the fifty shooting games and try them out—surely a video game wouldn't require Originium Arts just to pull the trigger.
Yukari had barely fired a few shots when she heard Ambriel whooping: "Hey, you're pretty good?! Great, great, keep going!" By the time Yukari had had her fill and came back to the side-scroller cabinet, she arrived just in time to see Makoto and Ambriel take the clear trophy on the final map.
"So what was it you wanted to buy, anyway?" Yukari asked on the way back to the dorm.
"Mm... a book cover, and maybe a glass flower arrangement." Makoto answered. "I think the Doctor and the class president would like that sort of gift. I'd like to give them before we go."
"Ah..."
"And I'd like to try other kinds of work, too."
"Still short on money?"
"And I want to see more of what happens in this city. We came all this way."
Yukari laughed. "So that's why you wanted to get a part-time job?"
Makoto did not answer; the dormitory was already before them. He pushed open the door, and the lounge felt at once familiar and unfamiliar—and he heard someone say, "Welcome back."

sections.title: Archive File 3
sections.text:
One afternoon Makoto came to my office and set down two gift boxes—one for me, he said, and one for the class president. They would be parting before long, and he wanted to thank us for looking after them. Amiya's spirits dipped a little; she had been avoiding the thought that Makoto and the others would soon leave. Still, she rallied quickly and said she would accept hers as a birthday present.
Learning that Amiya's birthday falls in winter, Makoto wished her a happy birthday in advance. We got to talking about Amiya's past birthdays, and the subject turned to when she was first taken in. Makoto did not seem surprised; he nodded and remarked that Lateran people seem fond of adopting children. I explained that Amiya was not adopted from the Revelation Home. He seemed to take some interest in the topic, so I told him a little more. Laterano's social environment is somewhat particular: a considerable share of its residents never form families at all, and so many Lateran children—Sankta especially—are sent from birth to the Revelation Home, Laterano's public institution for raising children. Some grow up there to adulthood; others are adopted. Because of empathy and Laterano's social system, Lateran people hold that every child is a child of God, whether raised at the Revelation Home or in a family. Whether that will change in the future, of course, no one can say for certain now.
Having heard all this, Makoto seemed to be thinking about something. Amiya, too, appeared curious about how he had grown up. She glanced at me first; I understood what she wanted, but I shook my head all the same.
Following on from that, I asked Makoto whether he would like to visit the Revelation Home. He hesitated a little, but agreed. There we also ran into a former student of mine, Spuria. She works in the Sixth Chamber now and happened to be visiting the friars that day. We played with the children for a while and helped the friars with a few chores; by the time we left, the sun was setting. Spuria had picked up that Makoto was a foreigner, and before parting she winked at him and said, "Places like this in Laterano are interesting, aren't they?" Makoto nodded. "Yes. The children all look happy."
On the way back to the dorm, Makoto told Amiya and me a few amusing stories about life with his friends in the Iwatodai dormitory of Gekkoukan High School. Fighting Shadows is grueling work, but day to day those children lead plain, simple student lives in that dorm. The steadiness in his voice seemed to let you feel the contentment in his heart.
At the dormitory door he said to us, "Doctor, Amiya—thank you for showing me around today." The moon, only just risen, made his figure look somehow insubstantial.
"There's no need to thank us, Makoto..." Amiya told him. She hesitated, then said it anyway: "I've always felt that... there's family you're given, and family you choose, and there isn't only one way to be happy... I chose the teacher as my family, and that is my happiness."
Makoto smiled softly. "Mm. I think so too."

sections.title: Archive File 4
sections.text:
Makoto said that since coming to Laterano, he had not dreamed once. He asked me whether that might be because coming to Laterano was itself a dream—since only within a dream does one not dream again.
I said to him: if I were a person in your dream, how do you think I would answer?
Afterwards I walked with Makoto around the city of Laterano—some places he had likely already seen, others I guessed he had not. We went through the shopping street where Amiya and I usually buy things, dropped by the bookshop I frequent, listened to someone playing a violin in the square before the Papal Hall, passed the hospital where Kal'tsit works, looked down from the school roof at the apple blossoms below, walked past the funeral hall that has now formally opened, and finally came to the edge of the mobile city.
Looking at the low hills in the distance, you would think the mobile city was not moving very fast at all. I asked Makoto whether it still felt like a dream to him. He was quiet for a moment, then said no, not anymore—he had felt so much in this city. It was a good place.
It was only a small coincidence, I said. There are still a great many corners of this land, and if their journey had passed through those instead, it would surely have been far harder.
"Have you been to all those places?" he asked me. I answered that I had been to some, and that there were still many I had never set foot in.
"Will you go someday, Doctor?" Makoto went on to ask.
I said that I would.
Makoto smiled faintly. "This world outside Laterano... no, 'this land' seems to be quite vast. I hope I get the chance to see it. Perhaps I could even be of help to you, Doctor."
I nodded. The day of parting was drawing near, but why bring it up just then? The mobile city was still moving, night had not yet fallen, and when we speak of the future we may always hope that the journey stretches on into the distance.

sections.title: Encrypted Report
sections.text:
Makoto Yuki is without question the core of this group called the Specialized Extracurricular Execution Squad (S.E.E.S.); the other members call him "leader." From my observation of their battles, although all of these transfer students can summon a "Persona," Makoto appears to be the only one able to summon several different ones. Aigis's attention toward him also merits study: it is not ordinary friendship or trust (given that Aigis's self-awareness is incomplete), yet at present neither Makoto nor Aigis herself can explain it clearly. He carries a powerful will and is firmly set on returning to their original world, and that has driven the others to seek the way back without wavering. He truly is their leader, because he is thinking of these companions at every moment.
Makoto sometimes reminds me of Amiya. They are a little alike: both hold a powerful will and choose kindness without wavering. They may well protect a great many people—perhaps even save the fate of the world. But what a weight that is, and what does it mean for them? Only... even as I worry, I know that children like these will in the end walk the road few walk, and shoulder the choices they believe in. Not for themselves, but for others.
